sections.title: If you need help right now

questions.question: I feel like I am about to gamble right now. What should I do?
answer: Step away from your phone, your computer, or the place where you usually gamble, and tell someone you trust.
Open the “Assistance” section and write what you are feeling: it walks you through it step by step to bring the urge down.
Review your saved strategies and the commitment you signed: they are there for exactly this moment.
If the urge is very strong, call a family member, a friend, or your local emergency services.

questions.question: What should I do if I have thoughts of hurting myself?
questions.answer: That matters more than any result or record inside the app. If you feel you are in danger right now, contact your local emergency services or someone you trust immediately. The application is not an emergency service and does not replace crisis care. Inside the app you can write in the “Assistance” section, and if you have a Premium plan you can ask for a human agent from our team to step in.

questions.question: Can I talk to a real person instead of an automated assistant?
questions.answer: The “Assistance” conversation always starts with a virtual assistant. From there, Premium users can tap “Talk to a human agent” so our team joins the conversation. This option is not available on the free plan: if you need to reach a person, write to us from “Help and Support”. Our team is not available 24 hours a day, so in an emergency always turn to your local emergency services first.

questions.question: What is gambling addiction?
questions.answer: Gambling addiction is an impulse control disorder where a person cannot resist the need to gamble, even when it negatively affects their personal, work, family, or financial life.

questions.question: What are the most common signs that I have a gambling problem?
answer: Betting more money than you can afford to lose.
Lying to family or friends about the time or money spent gambling.
Trying to stop gambling without success.
Using gambling as an escape from problems, sadness, or stress.
Going into debt or borrowing money to keep gambling.

questions.question: Can gambling addiction be cured?
questions.answer: Gambling addiction is a disorder that can be controlled with professional help, personal commitment, and the right support. Many people are able to stop gambling and live a full life.

questions.question: What should I do if a family member or friend has gambling addiction?
questions.answer: The best approach is to support them without judgment, encourage them to seek help, and avoid lending them money to gamble. You can also guide them to use the application or contact a specialist.

questions.question: Does the application replace professional help?
questions.answer: No. The app is a support, reflection, and accompaniment tool, but it does not replace psychological therapy or medical treatment. It is not an emergency service either. We always recommend reaching out to health professionals.

questions.question: What will I find inside the app?
answer: Self-assessment forms with a results report.
Conversational assistance for difficult moments, with human support available on the Premium plan.
A relapse log with a conclusion and advice to get back on track.
A personal commitment you sign within the dopamine control module, with follow-up on your process.
Your own strategies and those shared by the community to stop gambling.
Debt tracking: creditors, installments, payments, and outstanding balance.
A community where you can share your experience, comment, and chat with other people.
Achievements that recognize your progress and participation.

questions.question: How does the Assistance section work? Am I talking to an artificial intelligence?
questions.answer: Yes, assistance runs on a virtual assistant powered by artificial intelligence, designed to accompany you and help you make sense of what you are going through. It is not a health professional and it does not provide diagnoses. On the Premium plan you can ask for a human agent from our team to join the conversation; in that case, that person reads the history of that conversation in order to help you.

questions.question: Can I use the application if I do not have gambling addiction?
questions.answer: Yes. The app is also useful if you want to learn about gambling addiction, support a loved one, or prevent risky behavior.

questions.question: What happens if I relapse?
questions.answer: A relapse does not mean failure: it is part of the recovery process. The app lets you record what happened (date, amount, emotion, and trigger), reflect on it, and receive a conclusion with advice to get back on track.

questions.question: What languages is the app available in, and how do I change the language?
questions.answer: The application is available in Spanish and English. You can change the language from your profile or from the language selector; the change applies to the whole app, including these frequently asked questions.

questions.question: Will the app send me notifications?
questions.answer: Yes. You will receive notifications about new messages in your chats, achievements you unlock, and reminders related to your process, such as due dates for the debts you have recorded. You can review them in the Notification Center.

questions.question: How do I create my account?
questions.answer: You can sign up with your email address and a password, or sign in directly with your Google or Facebook account. If you sign up with email, we will send you a 6-digit code to verify your address before you can use the app.

questions.question: I am not receiving the verification code. What should I do?
questions.answer: Check your junk or spam folder and make sure the address is spelled correctly. On the verification screen you can tap “Resend code” to get a new one. If it still does not arrive, write to us from “Help and Support” and tell us the email address you signed up with.

questions.question: I forgot my password. How do I recover it?
questions.answer: On the sign-in screen, go to “Recover password” and enter your email: we will send you a code to create a new password. If you signed in with Google or Facebook you do not have a password in our app, so you must sign in with that same button.

questions.question: Can I change my profile details?
questions.answer: Yes. From “Profile” you can update your personal details, your photo, and your nickname, which is the name the rest of the community sees.

questions.question: How do I delete my account and my personal data?
questions.answer: From “Profile”, in the danger zone, you can submit a data deletion request. Our team reviews it and confirms the outcome; if for some reason it cannot be applied, you will receive the reason. Deletion is permanent: your records, assessments, posts, and conversations are lost and cannot be recovered. If you have an active subscription, cancel it first so it does not renew.

questions.question: Is the application free?
questions.answer: Yes, you can use the app on a free plan. There is also a Premium plan with full access to every tracking and support tool.

questions.question: What exactly does the free plan include?
answer: Up to 10 community posts.
One conversation with assistance, with a maximum of 5 messages from you.
One signed commitment within the dopamine control module.
One relapse record.
Reading and voting on community strategies, without being able to create your own.
Self-assessment forms and human agent assistance are reserved for the Premium plan.

questions.question: What do I get with the Premium plan?
answer: Posts, assistance conversations, commitments, and relapse records without the free plan limits.
Assistance with support from a human agent on our team.
Access to the self-assessment forms and their reports.
The ability to create your own strategies.
Priority in support and in the follow-up of your case.

questions.question: Is there a free trial?
questions.answer: Yes. The first time you subscribe you get a 7-day free trial of the Premium plan, and you can cancel during that period if you decide not to continue.

questions.question: What plans are available and how can I pay?
questions.answer: You can choose a monthly, quarterly, semiannual, or annual plan; longer plans are discounted against the monthly price. Payments are processed through Stripe, our payment gateway, and you can use a credit card, a debit card, or supported digital wallets. We do not store your card details.

questions.question: How do I cancel my subscription?
questions.answer: From the subscription section you can cancel automatic renewal at any time. You do not lose access immediately: you keep Premium features until the expiry date of the period you already paid for, and after that your account returns to the free plan.

questions.question: If I go back to the free plan, do I lose what I recorded?
questions.answer: No. Your information (relapses, debts, commitments, posts, and strategies) stays in your account. What applies again are the free plan limits for creating new content and access to Premium-only features.

questions.question: I have a problem with a charge, or I want to request a refund
questions.answer: Write to us from “Help and Support” with the date of the charge and the plan you purchased, and we will review your case together with our payment gateway. If what you want is to avoid the next charge, simply cancel automatic renewal from the subscription section.

questions.question: Who sees what I post in the community?
questions.answer: Everything you post in the community is visible to other people using the app, along with your nickname and profile photo. Do not post details you would not want to share, such as your address, your phone number, or your account information.

questions.question: Can I participate anonymously?
questions.answer: Your posts always appear with your profile nickname and photo, not anonymously. If you prefer not to be identifiable, choose a nickname that is not your real name and a photo that does not expose you.

questions.question: What content is not allowed?
answer: Promoting betting, casinos, or any gambling platform.
Sexual content.
Violence.
Harassment, insults, or hate speech.
Content that encourages self-harm or suicide.
Spam, scams, or attempts to sell products and services.

questions.question: How do I report a post?
questions.answer: In the post menu, choose “Report post”, select the reason, and add details if you want. Your report is confidential: the person who posted is not told who reported them. When five different people report the same post, it stops being publicly visible while the administration reviews it.

questions.question: Someone reported my post. What happens now?
questions.answer: While it is under review, only you and the administration can see the post. After the review, it is either restored and becomes public again, or permanently removed if it breaks the community rules. If an account accumulates several removed posts, it may be shut down.

questions.question: Can I chat with other people?
questions.answer: Yes. You can start one-to-one conversations with other users or create group chats. Keep in mind that everyone taking part in a chat can read everything you write there.

questions.question: What is the debt tracker for?
questions.answer: It keeps your creditors, amounts, interest, installments, and payments in one place, so you can see how much you still owe and when your next payment is due. The application is not a financial institution: it does not charge, lend, or process real payments; it only organizes the information you enter, so its accuracy depends on the data you record.

questions.question: What is the dopamine control commitment?
questions.answer: It is a personal statement where you identify the games that affect you, your reasons for quitting, and the actions you will take, and that you sign inside the app. It is a commitment to yourself, with motivational and follow-up value; it is not a legally binding document.

questions.question: Why should I record my relapses?
questions.answer: Recording a relapse helps you spot patterns: when it happened, how much money was involved, and which emotion and trigger were behind it. With that information you receive a conclusion with recommendations and, over time, you can see your own progress.

questions.question: What are strategies and who can see them?
questions.answer: They are concrete resources that help you avoid gambling. When you create a strategy you choose whether to share it with the whole community or keep it private; private ones are visible only to you. You can also vote on other people’s strategies to highlight the most useful ones.

questions.question: What are achievements?
questions.answer: They are recognitions you unlock as you progress and take part in the community. You will get a notification when you earn a new one, and you can see them all in the “My Achievements” section.

questions.question: What are donations?
questions.answer: They are voluntary contributions you can make to sustain the community and fund the subscription prizes raffled among users. They are entirely optional: they do not affect your access to the app or your recovery process.

questions.question: Is my personal data safe?
questions.answer: Yes. Your information is transmitted and stored securely, and access is restricted to authorized staff who need to review it in order to provide the service. We never sell your data, and we never share it with betting companies, advertisers, or insurers.

questions.question: Who can see my information inside the app?
answer: Only you can see your debts, your relapses, your commitments, your private strategies, and your form results.
Your posts, comments, and public strategies are visible to the rest of the community.
Chat messages are visible to the people taking part in that conversation.
Assistance conversations are processed by our virtual assistant; if you request human support, the agent from our team handling your case reads that conversation.
The administration can review reported posts, messages sent to support, and data deletion requests.

questions.question: Do you share my data with third parties?
questions.answer: We do not sell your information and we do not share it for advertising purposes. We do work with providers that make the service possible and that process data on our behalf: Stripe handles subscription payments, and an artificial intelligence provider processes assistance conversations. These providers may only use that data to deliver that service to us.

questions.question: Does the app track my location?
questions.answer: No. The application does not access your location or track your movements.

questions.question: I share my phone with someone else. How do I protect my information?
questions.answer: Sign out when you finish using the app, protect the device with a passcode or your fingerprint, and do not save your password in a shared browser. Keep in mind that anyone with access to your open session can see your personal records.

questions.question: What should I do if I have a technical problem or a suggestion?
questions.answer: Go to “Help and Support” and use the form to describe what happened: a technical failure, a problem with your account or subscription, or a suggestion to improve the app. Our team reviews every message and contacts you at your account email address.

questions.question: How long does it take to get a reply?
questions.answer: We review every message in the order it arrives, prioritizing Premium users and urgent cases. We are not available 24 hours a day, so if it is an emergency, turn to your local emergency services or to someone you trust.

questions.question: Where can I find professional help outside the application?
questions.answer: We recommend talking to your primary care doctor or a psychologist specialized in addictions, and looking up your country’s public mental health services and gambling support groups, such as Gamblers Anonymous, which exist in many cities and also online. In a situation of immediate risk, contact your local emergency services.

questions.question: Where can I read the terms of use and the privacy policy?
questions.answer: You can review them at any time from the legal information section of the app. If you have questions about how we handle your information or want to exercise your rights over your data, write to us from “Help and Support”.

community.title: To the Community
community.subtitle: Help fund the giveaway prizes.
community.description:
Community donations work as follows: randomly selected users browsing the site will be eligible to win a percentage of your donation. They will receive a notification that they have a chance to win a prize.

The formula is simple: (donated amount / monthly subscription price = number of subscription months to be awarded). For example, if your donation is $100 and the subscription cost is $5 per month, the number of subscription months to be awarded will be 20.

Spin for users without a subscription:

1 free month of subscription (40% probability)
2 free months of subscription (30% probability)
3 free months of subscription (15% probability)
5 free months of subscription (10% probability)
12 free months of subscription (5% probability)

The amount you choose to donate will be distributed among the community and will depend on the randomness of the machine that will decide which users can win the subscription months.

The Spin that will appear will be the following:

DebtPolicy.title: Debt Information
DebtPolicy.policy:
Information Confidentiality

• All entered data (amount, creditor, dates, payments) are private and only visible to the user.
• The application will not share or sell this information to third parties.

Use of Information

• The registered information will be used solely for personal debt control within the application.
• Calculations, reminders, and generated reports have an informative purpose and support for the user.

Data Accuracy

• The user is responsible for correctly entering amounts, dates, and creditors.
• The application assumes no responsibility for errors in information registered by the user.

Notifications and Reminders

• The system may send notifications or alerts related to debt maturities, payments, or reports, as long as the user allows it.

Limitation of Liability

• The application is not a financial entity, nor does it collect or manage real payments.
• Its function is solely to organize and facilitate the control of personal debts.
